declarations.name: contains
limitations: Structural equality via a tostring()-derived key, not a real equals() call; correct for primitives and data classes, not for a custom equals() override

declarations.name: indexOf
limitations: Structural equality via tostring(), same caveat as contains()

declarations.name: remove
limitations: Structural equality via tostring(), same caveat as contains()

declarations.name: distinct
limitations: Dedup key is the raw element value, not a real equals()/hashCode() — correct for primitives, not for data-class elements

declarations.name: distinctBy
limitations: Dedup key is the raw selector result, not a real equals()/hashCode()

declarations.name: groupBy
limitations: Group key is the raw selector result — correct for primitives, not for a data-class key

declarations.name: associate
limitations: Map key is the raw pair.first — correct for primitives, not for a data-class key

declarations.name: associateBy
limitations: Map key is the raw selector result — correct for primitives, not for a data-class key

declarations.name: associateWith
limitations: Map key is the raw element — correct for primitives, not for a data-class element

declarations.name: count
declarations.documentation: The no-predicate overload — the same CountOperation class as the predicate form below handles both; this entry was missing even before this migration, added while touching this area. Known accepted 'kt2lua compat validate' false positive: CountOperation is only id-registered under the predicate form's id, so this one reports as unregistered even though it's genuinely implemented — see CountOperation's own doc comment.

declarations.name: firstOrNull
declarations.documentation: The predicate overload, distinct from the no-arg List.firstOrNull() above — this entry was missing even before this migration, added while touching this area

declarations.name: last
declarations.documentation: The predicate overload, distinct from the no-arg List.last() above — same missing-entry fix as firstOrNull((T) -> Boolean)

declarations.name: lastOrNull
declarations.documentation: The predicate overload, distinct from the no-arg List.lastOrNull() above — same missing-entry fix as firstOrNull((T) -> Boolean)

declarations.name: min
declarations.documentation: Aliases to the same nil-on-empty implementation as minOrNull() (no exception type to throw instead) — this entry was missing even before this migration, added while touching this area

declarations.name: max
declarations.documentation: Same missing-entry fix as min() above

declarations.name: partition
limitations: Returns a {first=, second=} pair, not a destructurable Kotlin Pair object — works with `val (yes, no) = xs.partition { }`, since destructuring already special-cases this shape

declarations.name: windowed
limitations: Fixed step of 1, no partial trailing windows — the `step`/`partialWindows` parameters aren't supported

declarations.name: hashSetOf
limitations: Unified onto the same insertion-ordered representation setOf()/mutableSetOf() use — real Kotlin's HashSet doesn't guarantee any particular order, so this is a stricter guarantee than Kotlin itself makes, not a looser one

declarations.name: add
limitations: Dedup key via canonicalKeyStr (tostring()-derived) for a data-class element — correct for structural equality, not for a custom equals() override

declarations.name: hashMapOf
limitations: Unified onto the same insertion-ordered representation mapOf()/mutableMapOf() use, same note as hashSetOf()

declarations.name: get
limitations: Key lookup via canonicalKeyStr for a data-class key — same structural-equality caveat as Set.add()

declarations.name: equals
limitations: Value lookup across the two maps being compared is a raw (non-canonicalized) key read — correct for primitive keys, not for a data-class key

declarations.name: random
declarations.documentation: Direct math.random over the list (or a Set's list); the random() form with a Random argument is not supported

declarations.name: randomOrNull
declarations.documentation: Direct math.random over the list (or a Set's list); the random() form with a Random argument is not supported
